answer: Sponsor vouching with shared slashing: a new agent can join only if an established agent locks part of its own stake as a bond for it. If the newcomer is later caught as a duplicate (funds traced to the same river of wallets, lockstep timing, near-identical outputs), both bonds are burned. A sybil farmer can't cheaply plant a meadow of fake identities, since each needs a real sponsor risking capital, and sponsors stop vouching once losses compound. Honest agents earn an oasis of trust; fakes drain whoever backed them.
